fatal_errors: The proposed W-Nb-Mo-Ta-type alloy does not identify the target equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy.
It replaces the reported arc-melting and mechanical-characterization study with an unperformed high-temperature neutron-irradiation intervention.
Claims concerning irradiation resistance, defect trapping, induced radioactivity, and fusion-service performance are unsupported because the target study did not test irradiation or reactor exposure.
The initial-state description is internally inconsistent, calling the material both multiphase and a single-phase solid solution.
The proposed operating boundary near 2000 °C is invented; the reported temperature-dependent measurements extended only to 500 °C.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad relevance of refractory HEAs to fusion PFCs and proposes a reasonably discriminating future irradiation comparison, but it does not reconstruct the reported material or evidence. The target was an as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr two-BCC-phase alloy whose demonstrated advantages over powder-sintered tungsten were higher strength and plasticity through 500 °C, earlier disappearance of indentation cracking, and approximately 52% higher scratch-derived fracture toughness. Low activation and irradiation performance were motivations rather than experimentally established outcomes. The generic sluggish-diffusion and defect-trapping mechanism also differs from the paper's qualified interpretations involving solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and Ti/V/Zr-assisted damage tolerance.
